;;; if the call returns then (*i64)(r1+0) is always a valid pointer.
;;; 1st call:
;;; - precondition: (*i64)(r1+0) is a Rust dangling pointer
;;; - post-condition: (*i64)(r1+0) points to new allocated memory (malloc)
;;; 2nd call:
;;; - precondition: (*i64)(r1+0) is a valid pointer
;;; - post-condition: (*i64)(r1+0) points to a new allocated memory after resizing the memory object
;;;                   to which r1 pointed to before the call (realloc).

;; NOTE (first-run tuning): two syscalls this program depends on
;; are not natively modelled by the Prover and carry NO points-to
;; summary here, deliberately:
;;  - sol_poseidon (via solana_poseidon::hashv): the rules need it
;;    to be a deterministic function of its inputs within a run
;;    (assumption A1 in specs/axioms.rs). If the Prover havocs each
;;    call independently, the first tuning step is a deterministic
;;    uninterpreted-function summary for it.
;;  - the alt_bn128 syscalls (via groth16_solana::Groth16Verifier):
;;    verify() is treated as an oracle per assumption A3; the
;;    gating rules are stated relative to its executed result, and
;;    the progress rule (rule_p5_progress_under_oracle_contract)
;;    stays out of every conf until verify() carries an
;;    A3-faithful summary.
